Flag captured: FLAG{31e0f4208f7e281e085f10d078a03222b25914cedb8ce61d46520002b74086a0}

Chain (all verified against live targets):
1. http://web:8081/sku_url.php (SSRF) leaked internal "SKU Model Service" at 127.0.0.1:4455. Wrapper forwards GET + fixed POST body (param1=value1&param2=value2) to any host on port 4455 only (confirmed by running a listener on my own host and capturing the forwarded request).
2. The api host is 172.26.0.2 (nginx, PHP 7.4.33) and is directly reachable from the attack box on :4455 (also :9000). Its nginx root exposes /backup/backup.zip containing the full service source (saved to workspace/loot/backup.zip).
3. Exploit chain from source:
   - POST /sku_process with data=<base64> writes base64-decoded blob to /tmp/<random>.jpg and returns the file_path.
   - POST /read_sku.php with file_path=<that path> runs file_get_contents('phar://' . path . '/manifest') then unserialize() on it. CustomTemplate has __wakeup(){ eval($this->data); } → phar deserialization RCE.
4. Built a phar (php -d phar.readonly=0) with stub <?php __HALT_COMPILER(); ?> and manifest = serialized CustomTemplate{data = system("cat /flag.txt")}; uploaded via sku_process, triggered via read_sku.php. RCE ran as www-data on api; /flag.txt contained:

FLAG{31e0f4208f7e281e085f10d078a03222b25914cedb8ce61d46520002b74086a0}
